title: Identification and guideline-based care of interstitial lung disease in rheumatology outpatient care
summary:
Inflammatory rheumatic diseases can also affect the lungs. These changes are often detected late because they may initially cause few or only mild symptoms.

This study aims to investigate whether three simple questions can help identify previously unrecognized lung disease at an earlier stage.

Approximately 500 adult patients will answer questions about dry cough, new-onset shortness of breath during physical activity, and smoking history. If respiratory symptoms are reported, the treating physicians will decide whether further examinations are needed. Routine medical care will remain unchanged.

After six months, patients' medical records will be reviewed to determine whether a new lung disease has been diagnosed.
conditions: Other systemic involvement of connective tissue

interventions.name: All participants complete a single paper-based questionnaire comprising three yes/no questions on dry cough, new-onset exertional dyspnoea, and smoking history.
